draft.title: Health-related fitness
card: the most oxygen the body can take in and use each minute during hard exercise. It supports heart and lung health.
the most force a muscle or muscle group can produce in one effort. Muscular endurance is the ability to keep working against a lighter load for a long time.
the range of movement at a joint. It helps people move freely and may lower the chance of some injuries.
Each type of fitness depends on factors such as age, sex and training. For example, aerobic power usually falls with age, and training can improve all four.
draft.remember: Aerobic power, strength, endurance and flexibility each support health, and age, sex and training all shape them.

opts: Working against a light load for a long time
Producing the most force possible in one effort
Taking in and using the most oxygen each minute
Moving a joint through its full range of motion
a.why: Muscular endurance is the ability of a muscle to keep working for a long time against a lighter load. Muscular strength is tempting, but it is about the most force in a single effort.
a.clue: Think about how long the muscle keeps working, not how hard it works once.

b.q: Sam is 60 and starts a regular walking and jogging program. After three months, what is the most likely change in his aerobic power?
opts: It stays the same because he is 60
It falls because of his age
It becomes unrelated to his heart health
b.why: Training can improve aerobic power at any age. Age usually lowers aerobic power over time, but it does not stop training from improving it.
b.clue: Which factor on the card can Sam change?

a.best: Working against a light load for a long time
